purpose: Diagnose the immutable P9B s03 90-second timeout after the s02 fixture syntax defect was corrected. The diagnostic bounds only the external task-invocation child process, reads the existing ephemeral capture after a child timeout, and classifies whether the real task completed before the process failed to terminate or whether execution stalled earlier.

p9bLifecycleDiagnostic.diagnosticMethod: fixture-only replay of the frozen base physical source with the already-diagnosed generated-preload newline escaping correction plus a 45000ms timeout on only the child task-invocation process; after timeout the pre-existing ephemeral capture is classified before cleanup
p9bLifecycleDiagnostic.successMeaning: The diagnostic successfully bounds and classifies the child lifecycle state with clean physical cleanup. A diagnostic PASS is not P9B physical validation and does not by itself authorize a product change.

invariants: P9B s01 s02 and s03 evidence remain immutable
Computer Use product remains unchanged during diagnosis
Computer Control remains unchanged during diagnosis
external invocation carries only version task resources
resource provenance is explicit and is not inferred from UI state
provider selection remains Computer Use-owned and lazy
no screenshot OCR payload or coordinates are persisted

promotionOnPass.next: If the task reached VERIFIED_SUCCESS before child timeout, localize and fix the task-invocation process lifecycle forward-only, then contract-test the cleanup boundary before a new physical session. Otherwise diagnose the last observed execution stage without weakening the physical contract.

nonClaims: A diagnostic PASS does not make P9B PHYSICALLY_VALIDATED
The diagnostic does not validate the default interactive CLI
The diagnostic does not authorize generic Pulsar behavior
The diagnostic does not authorize UI-derived resource provenance
The diagnostic does not change Computer Control ownership of delivery mechanics
The diagnostic does not weaken CLICK_POSTED != success
